pluss::note::rand_between¶

Back to Note Factory API Reference

Signatures¶

Note pluss::note::rand_between(string_view lo, string_view hi,
                               integer_range sizes, std::uint64_t seed = 0)
Note pluss::note::rand_between(string_view lo, string_view hi,
                               std::initializer_list<std::int64_t> sizes,
                               std::uint64_t seed = 0)

Random Single Characters From A Chosen Range¶

rand_between() fills a Note of shape sizes with single characters drawn uniformly from the inclusive ASCII range [lo, hi]. Where rand is fixed to the alphabet, rand_between lets you name the endpoints: digits "0"–"9", a hex-nibble set "0"–"f" (with the gap characters included — see below), a punctuation band, an arbitrary slice of the ASCII table.

Parameters¶

  • lo, hi — each exactly one ASCII character (code point 0x00–0x7F). They are the inclusive bounds of the draw, read as byte values. lo must be <= hi.

  • sizes — the output shape, same rules as full: an initializer_list or any contiguous std::int64_t range, empty for a scalar, non-negative extents, rank at most three.

  • seed — the PRNG seed, with the same contract as rand: a non-zero seed is fully deterministic for a given lo, hi, and sizes; seed 0 (default) draws fresh entropy each call.

The draw is over contiguous code points, not over a curated character class. rand_between("0", "z", …) therefore includes :, ;, A–Z, [, and so on — every byte between '0' (0x30) and 'z' (0x7A). Choose lo and hi so the whole span is acceptable, or post-filter the result.

The result is UTF-8 mode.

Example 1: A Column Of Random Digits¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::rand_between("0", "9", {10}, 5))
          << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[10], dim=1, numel=10, encoding=utf8)
["6", "0", "8", "2", "4", "1", "3", "9", "8", "6"]

Ten independent draws from '0'..'9' inclusive, fixed by seed 5.

Example 2: A Lower-Case Letter Block¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::note::rand_between("a", "z", {2, 3}, 5);
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 3], dim=2, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["w", "a", "i"], 
  ["c", "u", "r"]
]

Any rank up to three; draw order is row-major.

Example 3: lo Greater Than hi Is Rejected¶

try {
  pluss::note::rand_between("z", "a", {3}, 1);
} catch (const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string msg(e.what());
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

pluss::note::rand_between: expected lo <= hi

Example 4: A Multi-Character Bound Is Rejected¶

try {
  pluss::note::rand_between("ab", "z", {3}, 1);
} catch (const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string msg(e.what());
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

pluss::note::rand_between: expected a single ASCII character

Each bound must be exactly one ASCII character.
